p: By playing The Shift, using its website, instructor dashboard or review pages, or creating an account, you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, don't use The Shift. "We" and "us" mean The Shift and its creator.

The Shift is a game for practicing clinical judgment. It is provided for general education and entertainment. It is not medical, nursing, pharmacy, legal or other professional advice, and using it does not create any nurse–patient, provider–patient or other professional relationship.

It is not a substitute for an accredited nursing program, clinical instruction, preceptorship, continuing education requirements, your licensing board's rules, your employer's or school's policies, or the judgment of a licensed professional.

Do not use anything in The Shift to make decisions about the care of a real person. Medication doses, protocols, nomograms, lab values and thresholds, scoring, timing and the legal framework are simplified and adapted for teaching. They may differ from current clinical guidelines, manufacturer labeling, your facility's protocols and the law where you live or work.

In real practice, follow the orders you're given, your facility's policies and procedures, current drug references and the scope of practice in your state. If you have a question about your own health, talk to a qualified health professional. In an emergency, call 911.

Content is written to reflect commonly taught nursing practice as of its last update, and each shift shows whether it has been reviewed by a clinician. Even so, medicine and law change, reviewers can disagree, and errors happen. We don't promise that any content is accurate, complete, current or suited to your situation, and we may change or remove content at any time.
If you spot something clinically wrong, please tell us through Menu → Send feedback or report a problem.

The psychiatric shifts are written to California law (for example, 5150, 5250, 5585, Riese and LPS conservatorship) as one example. Other states' laws differ. A General US setting replaces those terms with plain descriptions, but neither version is a statement of the law where you practice. Facility policies also differ from unit to unit.

The Shift is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by the National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN). NCLEX®, NCLEX-RN® and NCLEX-PN® are registered trademarks of NCSBN, used here only to describe the exam the practice relates to. Practice questions are original and are not actual exam items. Using The Shift does not guarantee that you will pass any exam, course or competency check.

Shifts depict suicide risk, self-harm, child abuse, overdose, alcohol withdrawal, physical restraint, serious illness and death, written at the level a nurse would encounter them. Take a break whenever you need to. If you are thinking about harming yourself or are in crisis, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, US), or call 911.
The Shift is intended for adults (18 or older) in nursing education or practice. Younger learners may use it only with a parent's or educator's permission and supervision.

All patients, families, staff, hospitals, units and events in The Shift are fictional. Any resemblance to real people or events is coincidental. Please don't enter real patient information or anything that identifies a real person anywhere in the game, including feedback.

You're responsible for activity on your account. If you buy the shift pack, payment is handled by Stripe; contact us if something goes wrong with a purchase. Feedback and clinical review comments you send may be used to improve The Shift without any obligation or payment to you. How data is handled is described in the Privacy page.
